hero_image.prompt: A premium robotics textbook hero illustration of RoboRover, a compact two-wheel educational rover with a small front distance sensor, visible motors and battery compartment, positioned on a marked laboratory floor facing a cardboard box. Include subtle visual callouts showing three decision-authority possibilities: a human operator with a controller, a stored program represented inside the onboard computer, and an onboard sensor observing the box. Technically plausible educational hardware, realistic materials and lighting, restrained modern editorial style, clean composition, no decorative sci-fi elements, no watermark, minimal essential labels only.
hero_image.caption: RoboRover is the same physical robot whether a human, a stored program, or autonomous software selects its immediate actions.
hero_image.alt_text: Educational engineering illustration of a small wheeled rover with motors, computer, battery, front distance sensor, human controller, and cardboard box environment.

inline_visuals.prompt: Create a clean technical diagram explaining the course working description of a robot. Show a physical machine boundary around RoboRover, controlled actuators labeled at the wheels, an arrow showing physical task performance, and three separate sources of immediate action selection: human operator, preprogrammed controller, and autonomous software. Visually separate robot identity from decision authority. Premium robotics textbook style, clear arrows, restrained colors, minimal readable labels, no clutter.
inline_visuals.caption: Robot identity concerns the physical machine and its controlled task; decision authority may belong to a human, a preprogrammed controller, or autonomous software.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Diagram separating a robot's physical machine and actuators from the three possible sources of immediate action decisions.

inline_visuals.prompt: Create a compact comparison diagram with five technically accurate panels: timer-controlled traffic signal, thermostat, teleoperated rover, industrial robot arm, and autonomous vacuum. For each panel show physical system, immediate decision authority, and whether measured state affects the current or future action. Emphasize that a preprogrammed task and feedback can coexist. Do not use an automatic door. Premium editorial robotics education layout, precise icons and arrows, minimal text.
inline_visuals.caption: Different systems can have different decision authority and feedback behavior; robot identity and control mode are separate questions.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Five-panel technical comparison of a traffic signal, thermostat, teleoperated rover, industrial arm, and autonomous vacuum showing decision authority and feedback.

inline_visuals.prompt: Create a realistic engineering illustration of RoboRover moving a lightweight blue block toward a collection tray on a marked laboratory floor. Include a small measurement panel or diagram showing average speed 0.25 metres per second, elapsed time 8 seconds, and distance 2.00 metres, with units clearly arranged as a visual teaching aid. Show wheel contact with the floor and subtle indications that real wheel slip can make measured distance differ from the ideal model. Premium robotics textbook style, technically plausible, no clutter.
inline_visuals.caption: The ideal distance model multiplies average speed by elapsed time, while real wheel slip and changing conditions can create error.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Small wheeled rover pushing a blue block toward a tray, with a visual equation showing speed, time, and ideal distance plus wheel-slip caveat.

inline_visuals.prompt: Create a clean technical visualization of the Python lab: three position-versus-time traces for the same RoboRover hardware under human-directed, preprogrammed, and autonomous obstacle-response modes. Show forward commands as rising segments and stop commands as flat segments, with an obstacle symbol appearing during the autonomous run. Use a textbook graph style with axes in seconds and metres, restrained colors, clear legend, and no unsupported numerical labels beyond the described four-second experiment.
inline_visuals.caption: The simulation keeps the hardware and speed model fixed while changing who or what selects the commands.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Technical line graph comparing three RoboRover position traces over time for human-directed, preprogrammed, and autonomous command selection.
